description: Tokenizer splits on parentheses and spaces. read() parses tokens into nested lists (AST). evaluate() recursively evaluates: int returns itself; list treats first element as operator (+, *, -), evaluates operands post-order, then combines. run() chains tokenize -> read -> evaluate. Tested on (+ 1 (* 2 3)) and (- 10 (+ 1 2)), both yield 7.

steps.description: tokenize: replaces ( and ) with spaced versions, splits on whitespace. Returns flat list of tokens.
read: recursive descent parser. Pops first token. If '(', collects items until ')' via recursive read calls, returns list. Otherwise tries int conversion, falls back to string (symbol).
While loop builds list of sub-expressions by recursively calling read. Handles nested parentheses.

evaluate: if int, return it. Else list: op = first element, args = rest. values = [evaluate(a) for a in args] (post-order recursion). Then dispatch on op: + sums, * multiplies, - subtracts second from first. Unknown op raises NameError.
Post-order evaluation: children evaluated before parent combines them. values list holds already-evaluated operands.

steps.answer: op = '+', args = [1, 2]. values = [evaluate(1), evaluate(2)] = [1, 2]. Returns sum(values) = 3.
steps.question: In evaluate, what happens when x is a list like ['+', 1, 2]?

steps.description: run: chains tokenize -> read -> evaluate. Single function to parse and evaluate a string.

title: Scheme-Like Calculator: Evaluation as Recursion
